name: MEDALLION FINANCIAL CORP

priced.reason: book method needs rotce_override or final_growth

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: That the capital-structure story is being read as a negative when management is demonstrably buying value. The TruPS repurchase takes out $15.0 million of face at 73.66 cents, a $3.95 million gain, and buys a five-year standstill from an activist who also agrees to exit the common by year end - that is a competent, accretive transaction, and it is the second time this year management has turned the balance sheet to the common holder's advantage. Set against $84.7 million of cumulative capital return since 2022 on a $260 million market capitalisation, the picture is a management team compounding per-share value through a soft patch, and 1.09x tangible book is the wrong price for that.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Whether the accretion is larger than the dilution of claims. Compare the $3.95 million one-off TruPS gain and the buyback accretion against the $4.95 million a YEAR of new Series G dividends.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Yes, and the arithmetic settles it against the counter. The TruPS gain is a single $3.95 million item; the Series G is a $4.95 million ANNUAL charge, in perpetuity, resetting to the five-year Treasury plus 4.94% in 2030. So in year one the two roughly cancel and in every year afterwards the Series G alone exceeds the whole of the one-off gain. Worse, the gain lands in Q4 2026, which is precisely the quarter whose net income the previous pass nominated as the test ('a print below ~$7M confirms the trend rather than a CECL artifact') - so that test must now be run EX the $3.95 million, or the one-off will read as a recovery. The counter is right that management is acting competently and wrong that it changes the return available to the common.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The cost of equity, for the fourth time, and it still decides the sign. The 8.4% comes from a beta of 0.621 at R-squared 0.196 measured on a stock that trades $810 thousand a day; at that liquidity it is not a measurement, and the schema has no field to override it. At 8.4% the corrected gap is about +19% before the Series G and -10% after it; at a beta of 1.0 it is -10% and -32%. I also do not have Q3 2026, which has not been filed.

what_changed: BOTH observables the 2026-09-23 pass nominated and could not get have now arrived, and both go against the common. (1) THE SERIES G IS SIZED. Medallion Bank launched a reopening of its Series G preferred on 2026-09-22 and priced it on 2026-09-23: 2,200,000 shares at a $25 liquidation amount, an aggregate $55,000,000, with a 330,000-share over-allotment option, at 9.00% fixed to 2030-07-01 and then the five-year Treasury plus 4.94%. That is about $4.95 million a year of additional non-controlling-interest dividends ahead of the common - roughly 20% of the current run-rate earnings available to the parent - accruing from 2026-10-01 and payable from 2027-01-01. The prior pass wrote 'I could not size the Series G reopening, so I cannot quantify how much further the NCI dividend load rises'; it is $4.95 million, taking the annual load from about $9.3 million to roughly $14.3 million. (2) THE TRUPS AND THE ACTIVIST. On 2026-10-19 Medallion agreed with BIMIZCI Fund and ZimCal Asset Management to repurchase $15.0 million of trust preferred securities at 73.66% of face for $11.049 million, booking a gain of about $3.95 million in Q4 2026, with the Investor Parties accepting a five-year standstill and agreeing to dispose of their remaining common by 2026-12-31. Q3 2026 earnings have NOT yet been reported, so the net-income test the last pass set has not run.
consensus_case: At $11.32 Medallion trades at 1.09x the tangible book it actually reports ($10.38 a share on equity_now), which for a specialty consumer lender earning a current return on tangible common equity of roughly 10.3% against an 8.4% cost of equity is close to fair. The buyer gets a bank subsidiary originating recreation and home-improvement loans at record volumes, assets through $3.2 billion, and a management team returning capital hard: $40.6 million of buybacks and $44.1 million of dividends since 2022, $23.6 million of it this year. The market is declining to pay a premium because the earnings are going the wrong way and the capital structure keeps adding claims ahead of the common.
base_case_rationale: No sustainable ROTCE is supplied, for the fourth consecutive pass on this name, and the Series G pricing makes the refusal firmer rather than weaker. The engine's 22.6% is the mean of fiscal 2023-2025 returns; net income attributable to Medallion Financial Corp. was $12.398 million in H1 2026 against $23.083 million a year earlier, a 46% fall, which annualises to about $24.8 million on $240.8 million of tangible common equity - a current ROTCE of about 10.3%, BELOW the low end of the engine's own `unstable_rotce_17.9%_to_32.1%` range. The new Series G takes roughly a further $4.95 million off income attributable to the parent, i.e. about 2.1 percentage points of ROTCE, so the forward figure is nearer 8.2%. At the engine's 8.4% cost of equity, 10.3% justifies 1.303x tangible book against an actual 1.09x, a gap of +19%; at 8.2% it justifies 0.98x, a gap of -10%; at a beta of 1.0 (cost of equity 10.45%) those become -10% and -32%. The sign flips across inputs I cannot fix, so the verdict is the output.
key_risks: Net income attributable to the parent fell 46% year over year in H1 2026 and the engine's 22.6% 'sustainable' ROTCE is a fiscal 2023-25 average of a company that no longer exists
The Series G reopening adds about $4.95M a year of preferred dividends ahead of the common at 9.00%, roughly 20% of run-rate earnings to the parent and about 2.1 points of ROTCE
Recreation-lending net charge-offs of 3.25%-3.94% on 2024-25 vintages that are only part-seasoned, into a softening consumer
Q4 2026 will carry a one-off gain of about $3.95M on the TruPS repurchase, which will flatter the exact print the last pass nominated as its test
Goodwill and intangibles are 41% of reported book; strip them and the equity cushion is about $240M against $3.2bn of assets
$810K of average daily dollar volume - a position could not be exited quickly, and the 0.62 beta that sets the 8.4% cost of equity is measured on that tape
Fourth appearance in this screen (2026-09-01, 09-02, 09-23, 10-23), two of them opportunistic, on an unfixed defect
watch_for: Q3 2026 net income attributable to Medallion Financial Corp.: below about $7M confirms the trend
Q4 2026 read EX the roughly $3.95M TruPS gain - the headline will otherwise overstate the run rate
Whether the Series G over-allotment (330,000 shares, about $8.25M) was exercised, adding a further $0.74M a year
The recreation-lending net charge-off ratio: whether it holds below 4% or breaks above it
Whether ZimCal and BIMIZCI complete their exit from the common by 2026-12-31 as agreed
